sources.title: Abkommen Schweiz–China – Parmelin: «China hat noch immer gewisse Handelshemmnisse»
Freitag, 30. Oktober 2026: Das Wichtigste des Tages

en.title: Swiss and China Renew Free‑Trade Agreement
en.dek: Swiss Federal Councilor Guy Parmelin signed a renewed free‑trade agreement with China on 30 October 2026, reducing most Swiss tariffs while addressing remaining trade barriers.
facts: Guy Parmelin signed the agreement on 30 October 2026.
China will reduce most tariffs on Swiss goods.
The agreement includes provisions for Swiss investment in China.
It contains a system of mixed committees and an independent expert panel to enforce labor standards.
Swiss agricultural quotas remain unchanged under WTO rules.
body: Guy Parmelin signed the renewed free‑trade agreement with China on 30 October 2026, a move that follows a period of stalled negotiations. The agreement removes most tariffs on Swiss goods, according to Parmelin, while China will also reduce tariffs on Swiss products. Swiss agricultural quotas remain unchanged, a detail Parmelin said does not affect the Swiss agricultural sector.

Parmelin said the agreement includes concessions in the agricultural sector, limited to WTO‑bound quotas, and that no additional quotas were granted beyond those already in place. The agreement also covers Swiss investment in China, aiming to ease market access, according to Parmelin.

Parmelin noted that China has ongoing trade barriers and that these were discussed with Chinese Trade Minister Wang Wentao, a point he emphasized during the signing. He said the agreement provides a mechanism for addressing such barriers through mixed committees, which will monitor compliance. An independent expert panel can be convened in case of disputes, a feature Parmelin highlighted as a first for China.

This system is the first time China has agreed to such a framework, a fact Parmelin underscored. The agreement also contains a clause that requires both countries to respect International Labour Organization standards, a commitment both sides will monitor. Parmelin said the agreement was negotiated quickly after talks resumed, citing the return of protectionism as a factor.
en.context: The free‑trade agreement was renewed after a period of stalled negotiations, a development that Swiss officials say was accelerated by a global return to protectionism. The agreement aims to reduce trade barriers between Switzerland and China and includes provisions for Swiss investment and labor standards.
